name: Weighed Tree Radius
description: You are given a tree of $$$n$$$ vertices and $$$n - 1$$$ edges. The $$$i$$$-th vertex has an initial weight $$$a_i$$$. Let the distance $$$d_v(u)$$$ from vertex $$$v$$$ to vertex $$$u$$$ be the number of edges on the path from $$$v$$$ to $$$u$$$. Note that $$$d_v(u) = d_u(v)$$$ and $$$d_v(v) = 0$$$. Let the weighted distance $$$w_v(u)$$$ from $$$v$$$ to $$$u$$$ be $$$w_v(u) = d_v(u) + a_u$$$. Note that $$$w_v(v) = a_v$$$ and $$$w_v(u) \neq w_u(v)$$$ if $$$a_u \neq a_v$$$. Analogically to usual distance, let's define the eccentricity $$$e(v)$$$ of vertex $$$v$$$ as the greatest weighted distance from $$$v$$$ to any other vertex (including $$$v$$$ itself), or $$$e(v) = \max\limits_{1 \le u \le n}{w_v(u)}$$$. Finally, let's define the radius $$$r$$$ of the tree as the minimum eccentricity of any vertex, or $$$r = \min\limits_{1 \le v \le n}{e(v)}$$$. You need to perform $$$m$$$ queries of the following form: $$$v_j$$$ $$$x_j$$$ — assign $$$a_{v_j} = x_j$$$. After performing each query, print the radius $$$r$$$ of the current tree.
input_specification: The first line contains the single integer $$$n$$$ ($$$2 \le n \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$) — the number of vertices in the tree. The second line contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1, \dots, a_n$$$ ($$$0 \le a_i \le 10^6$$$) — the initial weights of vertices. Next $$$n - 1$$$ lines contain edges of tree. The $$$i$$$-th line contains two integers $$$u_i$$$ and $$$v_i$$$ ($$$1 \le u_i, v_i \le n$$$; $$$u_i \neq v_i$$$) — the corresponding edge. The given edges form a tree. The next line contains the single integer $$$m$$$ ($$$1 \le m \le 10^5$$$) — the number of queries. Next $$$m$$$ lines contain queries — one query per line. The $$$j$$$-th query contains two integers $$$v_j$$$ and $$$x_j$$$ ($$$1 \le v_j \le n$$$; $$$0 \le x_j \le 10^6$$$) — a vertex and it's new weight.
output_specification: Print $$$m$$$ integers — the radius $$$r$$$ of the tree after performing each query.
approach_summary: Build a Segment Tree over the array. Implement point update and associative range query operations in O(log N) time per query.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1783G — Weighed Tree Radius [57. Segment Tree (Point Update Range Query)]
topic_editorial.summary: Range queries and updates via Segment Tree.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The query operation is associative (e.g., sum, min, max, gcd). Any contiguous range $[L, R]$ can be decomposed into at most $O(\log N)$ canonical dyadic intervals represented by nodes in a binary tree.
topic_editorial.solution_walkthrough:
### Step 1: Tree Construction
We build a binary segment tree over array $A[1..N]$.
Each node covers a segment $[L, R]$. If $L = R$, the node stores $A[L]$. Otherwise:
$$\text{node.val} = \text{combine}(\text{left\_child.val}, \text{right\_child.val})$$

### Step 2: Point / Range Updates
To update position $pos$ with value $val$:
- Traverse down to the leaf node $[pos, pos]$.
- Update leaf value.
- Recompute ancestor values on the way back up in $O(\log N)$ time.

### Step 3: Range Query Processing
To query the associative aggregate on range $[qL, qR]$:
- If current segment $[L, R]$ is completely within $[qL, qR]$, return node value.
- If disjoint, return identity element.
- Otherwise, split and return $\text{combine}(\text{query}(left), \text{query}(right))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}((N + Q) \log N)$
  Building the segment tree takes $\mathcal{O}(N)$. Each point/range query and update traverses at most $4 \log N$ tree nodes, requiring $\mathcal{O}(\log N)$ time per query.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N)$
  A standard binary segment tree requires at most $4N$ nodes to represent elements up to index $N$.
